message: A "not tracked" read from `git ls-files` is blind to non-ASCII paths. core.quotePath defaults to TRUE, so a Hebrew filename or an em-dash directory prints C-quoted and octal-escaped, and a literal match against the real name never fires. Use `-z` when the consumer takes NUL, or `git -c core.quotePath=false` for a line-oriented read. The same escaping applies to `git status --porcelain` (v1) and `git diff --name-only`.
why: Measured 2026-09-09 on platform #11581: a lane classified two paths as untracked with `git ls-files`, moved them out of the worktree, ran `git add -A`, and recorded the moves as deletions. Four files were lost from the commit and restored by hand. Both paths carried non-ASCII characters, so the escaping made a fully tracked file read as absent. The escaping is a DISPLAY decision that silently changes the bytes a matcher sees, so 'not present in the output' answers 'not present under its escaped spelling', never 'not tracked'.
example_fix:
# WRONG - a tracked non-ASCII path reads as untracked
git ls-files | grep -qxF "$name" || mv "$name" ../

# RIGHT - NUL-delimited, no escaping at all
git ls-files -z | tr '\0' '\n' | grep -qxF "$name"

# RIGHT - line-oriented, escaping turned off for this invocation
git -c core.quotePath=false ls-files | grep -qxF "$name"

# BEST for one path - the exit code IS the answer, no text matching at all
git ls-files --error-unmatch -- "$name" >/dev/null 2>&1
